shortlist: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression

shortlist.label: Ganglion Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist, consistent with MRI findings

shortlist.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) on MRI, matching the described imaging findings

shortlist.label: Nodular Tenosynovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and may present as a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and may present as a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the radial side of the wrist with biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) and the location along the radial edge, where ganglion cysts are commonly found, supports this diagnosis. Additionally, the positive Phalen’s maneuver and Durkan’s test indicating median nerve compression are consistent with a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the mass and its location does not as strongly suggest this diagnosis as it does for a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
rejected.why: This condition is less common and the clinical presentation does not as closely match the described symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Nodular Tenosynovitis
rejected.why: The encapsulated nature and specific imaging characteristics of the mass are not as typical for nodular tenosynovitis.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are less likely given the specific location and imaging characteristics described, which are more suggestive of a ganglion cyst.
